name: Donna Summer
hook: A Boston singer working in Munich whose records with Giorgio Moroder, released by Casablanca, set disco's length and then its electronic future.
blurb: Donna Summer was born LaDonna Gaines in Boston in 1948 and moved to Germany in the late 1960s to sing in the musical 'Hair', and built her career in Munich with the producers Giorgio Moroder and Pete Bellotte. 'Love to Love You Baby' started as a modest Dutch release. Then in 1975 Neil Bogart of Casablanca Records asked for a longer version, and the result ran over 16 minutes and went to number two in the US in February 1976. The BBC would not promote it because of her moaning vocal. On 'I Feel Love' (1977) she sang high and light over Moroder's all-synthesizer backing, a sequenced Moog, recorded in a single take. It is one of the most influential dance records ever made. She died in 2012.
